concepts.label: OnDelete handler
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the deletion-triggered JavaScript entry point (`function OnDelete(meta) {...}`), the OnUpdate handler's counterpart, fired when a document is removed from the listened-to keyspace

concepts.label: Embedded SQL++ statement in a handler
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a SQL++ statement (here `DELETE FROM ... WHERE ...`) written literally inline inside an Eventing handler's JavaScript body and executed synchronously as part of handling one mutation; distinct from the bucket-binding read/write model because it operates on an unbound keyspace via query language rather than a KV alias

relations.subject: eventing:on-delete-handler
relations.evidence: The `OnDelete` handler listens to mutations or data changes within a specified user's source collection.

relations.subject: eventing:on-delete-handler
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - verb phrase for a handler containing a literal SQL++ statement in its JavaScript body, executed as part of the callback rather than through a bound bucket alias's KV API

relations.subject: eventing:embedded-sqlpp-statement
relations.evidence: Unlike the similar scriptlet [cascadeKvDeleteWithDoc](eventing-handler-cascadeKvDeleteWithDoc.md), which uses KV or the Data Service, the example on this page uses SQL++.

relations.subject: eventing:on-delete-handler
relations.evidence: The `OnDelete` handler checks if the `user_id` is greater than or equal do 100, and then triggers a SQL++ query to delete all user-related information.

notable_absence.finding: No relation could be extracted describing an atomic, platform-level cascade-delete or referential-integrity mechanism. The page's own contrast with the KV-based `cascadeKvDeleteWithDoc` scriptlet shows there are two independent, handler-authored implementations of 'delete related documents' - one via embedded SQL++, one via KV operations - and neither is described as transactional. The log evidence ('OnDelete: removed orphaned transactions for:') confirms per-user, per-mutation execution, not a batch/atomic cross-collection delete.

cross_component_finding: This page directly answers the batch's cascade-delete question: there is no distinct cross-document consistency primitive. 'Cascade delete' in Eventing is just business logic - an OnDelete handler synchronously issuing an embedded SQL++ DELETE statement against a second keyspace inside its own callback, filtered by a business condition (`user_id >= 100`) that is unrelated to any platform consistency guarantee. The embedded-SQL++-in-handler mechanism itself (as opposed to the bucket-binding KV read/write model used in every other page in this batch) is the one genuinely new structural primitive this page surfaces for the Eventing vocabulary.
